question: A 26-year-old African-American woman comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of a nonproductive cough and chest pain. The pain is sharp and worse when she breathes deeply. During this time, she has also had two episodes of hematuria. Over the past 6 months, she has had intermittent pain, stiffness, and swelling in her fingers and left knee. She had two miscarriages at age 22 and 24. Her only medication is minocycline for acne vulgaris. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 138/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows an erythematous rash on her face. There is mild tenderness over the metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally with no warmth or erythema. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opb: Low serum levels of C3 and C4
options.opd: Bilateral enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "26-year-old African-American woman" -> "presents with nonproductive cough and chest pain" -> "sharp pain worse with deep breathing" -> "episodes of hematuria" -> "intermittent pain, stiffness, and swelling in fingers and knee" -> "erythematous rash on face" -> "symptoms suggest autoimmune condition" -> "possible systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)" -> "SLE commonly associated with anti-histone antibodies" -> 85%

CHAIN: "26-year-old African-American woman" -> "presents with respiratory symptoms and hematuria" -> "joint pain and rash suggest autoimmune disease" -> "history of miscarriages raises suspicion for SLE" -> "SLE can lead to complement consumption" -> "low serum levels of C3 and C4 are common in SLE" -> 80%

CHAIN: "26-year-old African-American woman" -> "presents with joint pain and swelling" -> "tenderness over metacarpophalangeal joints" -> "no warmth or erythema suggests non-inflammatory process" -> "erosions of joints are more typical of rheumatoid arthritis" -> "less likely in this case" -> 60%

CHAIN: "26-year-old African-American woman" -> "presents with respiratory symptoms and hematuria" -> "chest pain and cough could indicate pulmonary involvement" -> "bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is common in sarcoidosis" -> "less likely given the autoimmune symptoms" -> 50%

CHAIN: "26-year-old African-American woman" -> "presents with hematuria and joint symptoms" -> "cytotoxic glomerular antibodies are associated with certain kidney diseases" -> "not typical for SLE or autoimmune conditions" -> "less likely in this context" -> 40%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including a nonproductive cough, chest pain, hematuria, joint pain, and an erythematous facial rash, suggest a systemic autoimmune condition. The combination of these symptoms, particularly the rash and joint involvement, raises suspicion for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). In SLE, it is common to find low serum levels of complement proteins C3 and C4 due to complement consumption in the setting of immune complex formation. Therefore, further evaluation is most likely to show low serum levels of C3 and C4.
